confidence_notes: I ran three web searches: one for the RBA rate and two for Bratislava prices. The price searches returned crowd-sourced cost-of-living aggregates (MyLifeElsewhere, Traveltables, Expatistan). Some of those figures date from 2023 and the sites disagree with each other. Those aggregates put a domestic 0.5 L beer at about €2.3-2.5, a cappuccino at about €2.3-2.9, an inexpensive meal at about €9.4-10.4 and a mid-range meal for two at about $48. I adjusted them upward for old-town tourist venues and for inflation since the figures were published. I found no direct cocktail or restaurant wine-by-the-glass data, so cocktail is set at about 2.5x beer and wine glass at about 1.35x beer, based on typical Central European relationships. All accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge for a July peak-season window. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings, so those anchors are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with Central European capitals of similar size. Bratislava is somewhat cheaper than Vienna and similar to or slightly above Budapest and Prague for restaurant prices. Its accommodation is moderately priced, with summer demand pushing 3-star rates up.
